trial_name.text: Study 401 (4-week seasonal allergic rhinitis pivotal trial)

citations.quote: one pivotal 4-week trial in subjects with SAR (Study 401)
one 4-week SAR study (401-identified as pivotal by sponsor)

design.text: Randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled, 4-week single dose-level trial in seasonal allergic rhinitis

citations.quote: one was a 4-week single dose-level trial conducted in patients with seasonal allergic rhinitis
The efficacy and safety of OMNARIS Nasal Spray were evaluated in 4 randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled clinical trials

population.text: Adolescents and adults 12 years and older with seasonal allergic rhinitis

citations.quote: Patients enrolled in the studies were 12 to 86 years of age with a history of seasonal or perennial allergic rhinitis, a positive skin test to at least one relevant allergen, and active symptoms of allergic rhinitis at study entry.

endpoint.text: Difference from placebo in change from baseline of average AM and PM reflective total nasal symptom score (r-TNSS) averaged over the first 2 weeks

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint in the seasonal allergic rhinitis trial was the difference from placebo in the change from baseline of the average of morning and evening reflective total nasal symptom score averaged over the first 2 weeks of treatment.

result.text: Reflective TNSS difference from placebo -0.90 (95% CI -1.36, -0.45); p<0.001

trial_name.text: Study 402 (6-week perennial allergic rhinitis pivotal trial)

citations.quote: one pivotal 6-week trial in subjects with PAR (Study 402)
one 6-week PAR study (402-identified as pivotal by sponsor)

design.text: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter (41 centers, US and Canada), 6-week trial in perennial allergic rhinitis

citations.quote: Study 402 was double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel group in design, conducted in 41 centers in the United States and Canada in patients 12 years of age and older with history of PAR

population.text: Patients 12 years and older with a history of perennial allergic rhinitis and positive allergen skin test

citations.quote: conducted in 41 centers in the United States and Canada in patients 12 years of age and older with history of PAR and positive sensitivity test to relevant allergen by skin test.

endpoint.text: Difference from placebo in change from baseline of average AM and PM reflective total nasal symptom score (r-TNSS) over 6 weeks

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint in the perennial allergic rhinitis trial was the difference from placebo in the change from baseline of the average of morning and evening reflective total nasal symptom score averaged over the 6 weeks of treatment.

result.text: Reflective TNSS difference from placebo -0.62 (95% CI -0.97, -0.28); p<0.001

indication.text: OMNARIS Nasal Spray is indicated for the treatment of nasal symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older.

citations.quote: OMNARIS Nasal Spray is indicated for the treatment of nasal symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older.

target_moa.text: Ciclesonide is a non-halogenated glucocorticoid pro-drug hydrolyzed in the nasal mucosa to the active metabolite des-ciclesonide (RM1), which has anti-inflammatory activity with glucocorticoid receptor affinity 120 times higher than the parent compound; corticosteroids affect multiple cell types and mediators involved in allergic inflammation.

citations.quote: Ciclesonide is a pro-drug that is enzymatically hydrolyzed to a pharmacologically active metabolite, C21-desisobutyryl-ciclesonide (des-ciclesonide or RM1) following intranasal application.
Des-ciclesonide has anti-inflammatory activity with affinity for the glucocorticoid receptor that is 120 times higher than the parent compound.
Corticosteroids have been shown to have a wide range of effects on multiple cell types
The active component of OMNARIS Nasal Spray is ciclesonide, a non-halogenated glucocorticoid

key_safety.text: Most common adverse events in 2-6 week trials in patients 12 and older (200 mcg vs placebo): headache 6.0% vs 4.6%, epistaxis 4.9% vs 2.9%, nasopharyngitis 3.7% vs 3.3%, ear pain 2.2% vs 0.6%.

summary.text: Ciclesonide nasal spray (OMNARIS) is a new molecular entity of the corticosteroid class, reviewed under a standard priority classification and approved first cycle on October 20, 2006 for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in patients 12 and older; no advisory committee was convened, and a deferred PREA pediatric growth study and an HPA-axis safety study were required/committed post-approval.
